profile.address: 1, Ramland Road, Orangeburg, Town of Orangetown, Rockland County, New York, 10962
profile.reading:
ORNY1 is fifteenfortyseven Critical Systems Realty's data center in Orangeburg, New York, in the Town of Orangetown in Rockland County, sited on 23 acres less than a mile from the New Jersey border and about 22 miles from Midtown Manhattan, a location chosen for proximity to the New York metro market while sitting outside the city's highest cost real estate. The operator's own site puts current building space at 232,000 square feet, with a second building planned that would bring the campus to 462,000 square feet total.

On power, 1547's marketing describes 24 megawatts provisioned in an N plus 2 configuration, alongside references to 12 megawatts on site today and an on site substation capable of supporting up to 50 megawatts total. The same materials elsewhere describe 2N and N plus 1 power availability, suggesting the campus offers tenants a choice of redundancy tiers rather than a single fixed configuration across the building. Because the operator's public description mixes a provisioned target, an on site current figure, and a substation ceiling without settling on one unambiguous current operating load, this page treats those numbers as descriptive of the site's power story rather than as a single confirmed capacity figure, and readers should treat the substation number in particular as a utility interconnection ceiling rather than a statement about installed or contracted IT load.

The facility is built for high density colocation, supporting cabinets drawing 10 kilowatts or more, well above the industry norm for general purpose colocation space, which points toward a tenant base doing compute intensive or high performance work rather than simple storage or light enterprise hosting. Connectivity is provided through roughly a dozen network providers on site, with the operator advertising 1 gigabit to 10 gigabit connectivity reaching other buildings across New York and New Jersey, positioning ORNY1 as an interconnection point for the broader tri state region rather than a single tenant facility. Security measures described by the operator include biometric access control, closed circuit video monitoring, mantraps, and a stated 15 minute emergency support response time, standard features for a facility marketed to enterprise and hyperscale tenants who require documented physical security controls as part of their own compliance obligations. No opening date or full tenant roster is published for the site.

reading.body:
ORNY1 sits 22 miles north of Manhattan in Rockland County, chosen for proximity to the New York metro market while remaining outside the city's highest cost real estate. The campus occupies 23 acres and currently houses 232,000 square feet of building space, with a planned second building that would bring it to 462,000 square feet total. The operator describes a substation capable of supporting up to 50 megawatts, though that figure represents a utility infrastructure ceiling rather than a statement of current IT load.

The operator publishes 24 megawatts provisioned under an N+2 redundancy scheme alongside a separate claim of 12 megawatts on site today, without settling on a single unambiguous current operating load. The facility is built for high density colocation, supporting individual cabinets drawing 10 kilowatts or more, which points toward compute intensive work rather than general storage or light hosting. At common AI training density of roughly 40 kilowatts per rack, the 12 megawatts currently on site would support approximately 300 racks, though this is an assumption about workload type rather than an operator claim.

ORNY1 is the second largest published-capacity facility in New York by the operator's own figures, though New York has only one other facility with published megawatts in the state's 31 mapped locations. The site connects to roughly a dozen network providers and markets itself as an interconnection point for the tri state region rather than a single tenant facility. No opening date or full tenant roster is published.
